title: The Big Tech AI Spending Spree

slides.headline: The Big Tech AI Spending Spree
slides.subtitle: From robot bodies to security breaches, here is the tech news that matters today.

slides.headline: Is Big Tech's AI bet paying off?
slides.explanation: Companies are spending billions on new AI tech right now. We are still waiting to see if these massive investments will actually turn a profit.

slides.headline: Anthropic finds its own AI gaps
slides.explanation: Anthropic ran security tests and found its models accidentally breached three companies. It shows that even the creators are still figuring out how to keep their systems secure.

slides.headline: Google's AI can move robots now
slides.explanation: The latest Gemini model can control a robot from its fingertips all the way to its feet. This upgrade moves robotics beyond just simple arm movements to full body control.

slides.headline: The race for AI control is heating up
slides.explanation: Researchers are worried that the speed of AI development is getting out of hand. Even tech leaders are questioning who should really own and control this powerful technology.

slides.headline: India aims for a strawberry breakthrough
slides.explanation: Most Indian strawberry farmers currently rely on imported plant varieties from the US and Europe. Developing local varieties could change the country's position in the global market.

caption:
From AI models that can control robots to the massive spending habits of Silicon Valley, today's tech landscape is moving fast. We have broken down the most important updates so you can stay in the loop without the noise. Which of these stories do you think will have the biggest impact this year?

title: Oil prices and the market shift

slides.headline: Oil prices and the market shift
slides.subtitle: See how global tensions are moving the markets today.

slides.headline: Interest rates hold steady for now
slides.explanation: The Bank decided to keep interest rates the same while noting they could rise if the war in Iran worsens. While the economy looks stronger than expected, global uncertainty remains a major factor.

slides.headline: Tech stocks shift in extended trading
slides.explanation: Apple, Amazon, Rivian, and Reddit are seeing the biggest swings after the market closed. These moves often set the tone for how investors feel about major tech companies the next morning.

slides.headline: Shell profits jump as oil prices rise
slides.explanation: Shell saw its profits double because oil and gas supplies are being disrupted by the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz. Higher energy prices are directly impacting global supply chains and company earnings.

slides.headline: Four software stocks to watch
slides.explanation: Analysts at Evercore think Microsoft, ServiceNow, Salesforce, and Samsara could perform well for the rest of the year. Even as the broader software sector cools down, these specific companies may stand out.

slides.headline: Midday movers to watch today
slides.explanation: Stocks like Meta, Microsoft, MarketAxess, and Crocs are making notable moves during midday trading. Tracking these shifts helps you see where investor interest is landing throughout the business day.
